title: Ernest Hemingway Birthplace Museum

services.name: Field Trips
services.desc: We invite educators and students to the Ernest Hemingway Birthplace Museum for a unique learning experience. Students are welcomed into the restored Victorian home as it looked in 1890. Tours can be modified based on education levels (elementary/middle/high school/college) and class course objectives. Further, on request, we can draw out additional themes that may dovetail with your curriculum objectives, such as local history, Victorian living, the Civil War (Hemingway’s grandfathers), and WWI. Influences Hemingway incorporated into his writing: art, music, nature, and science We begin the tour in the parlor as students gather for a short story discussion of “A Day’s Wait” (grades 5-8).

services.name: Admission
services.desc: Due to the limited capacity on tours, we recommend that you purchase tickets in advance. If you choose to show up without purchasing tickets in advance we may not be able to accommodate you and your group. You can schedule and confirm your tour in advance by completing the information below. Please note if you are reserving more than one admission type, (Adult or Senior/Student) you will need to purchase each type separately. Otherwise, to select more than one admission, click date and time to add a reservation and repeat before clicking continue) When you arrive you can check-in with our reception desk (please bring your email confirmation just in case) prior to your scheduled tour time.

blurb: Ernest Hemingway's Birthplace Museum is nestled just west of downtown Chicago in Oak Park, Illinois. This is the ideal place to begin exploring the roots of the author's life and work. It is here that Ernest Hemingway was born in a second-floor bedroom on July 21, 1899.
